'''Omizunu''' ({{langx|ja|淤美豆奴神, 意弥都奴||Great Water Master}}), also known as '''Yatsukamizu Omitsuno''' ({{lang|ja|八束水巨津野}}) was a [[kami|Japanese deity]],<ref name="Antoni">{{cite journal |last1=Antoni |first1= Klaus |title=Izumo as the 'Other Japan': Construction vs. Reality |url=https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=f4c1688482fde5c4fbd16a8192d81decc6e97f93 |journal=Japanese Religions |volume=30 |issue=1&2 |pages=1–20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Tanabe |first=George J. Jr |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IdPgDwAAQBAJ&dq=Omizunu&pg=PA115 |title=Religions of Japan in Practice |date=2020-06-30 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-21474-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Kitagawa-2021">{{Cite book |last=Kitagawa |first=Joseph Mitsuo |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MzQGEAAAQBAJ&dq=Omizunu&pg=PA55 |title=On Understanding Japanese Religion |date=2021-02-09 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-22423-7 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Yatsukamizu Omitsuno">{{Cite web |title=Yatsukamizu Omitsuno • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/yatsukamizu-omitsuno/ |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo/Exhibition/Myths in the Izumo Province |url=https://www.izm.ed.jp/english/shinwa4.html |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=www.izm.ed.jp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=大水神 - Omizunu |url=https://japanese-culture.info/essays/legends/omizunu/ |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=英語対訳で読む日本の文化 |language=ja}}</ref><ref name="The Legend of Kunibiki">{{Cite web |title=The Legend of Kunibiki |url=https://www2.matsue-ct.jp/tp/the%20legend%20of%20kunibiki.html |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=www2.matsue-ct.jp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-01 |title=Episode 16: Susano'o Slays the Serpent... and does a bunch of other stuff |url=https://sengokudaimyo.com/podcast/episode-16 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=Sengoku Daimyo |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Cho-2022">{{Cite journal |last1=Cho |first1=Ilsoo |last2=一水 |first2=趙 |date=2022 |title=Korea in the Kamiyo: Locating Korea in the Age of the Gods Narratives in Early Modern Japan |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/48696751 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=49 |issue=1 |pages=1–20 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.49.1.2022.1-20 |issn=0304-1042 |jstor=48696751|s2cid=253607811 |doi-access=free }}</ref> the great-great-grandson of [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]].<ref>{{cite thesis |first1=Ilsoo David |last1=Cho |year=2017 |title=Discourses of Nation: Tensions in Early Modern Korea-Japan Relations |degree=PhD |publisher=Harvard University |url=https://dash.harvard.edu/bitstream/handle/1/41142069/CHO-DISSERTATION-2017.pdf}}</ref><ref name="fountainhead-local">{{cite book |last=Herbert |first=J. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Sg_JBQAAQBAJ&pg=PT402 |title=Shinto: At the Fountainhead of Japan |publisher=Taylor & Francis |year=2010 |isbn=978-1-136-90376-2 |series=Routledge Library Editions: Japan |page=402 |access-date=2020-11-21}}</ref>{{rp|277–278}} He was illustrated as a deer with a tree sprouting from it one the ''[[Mandala]] of the [[Kasuga-taisha]].''

He is known for expanding the [[Izumo Province]]<ref name="Antoni" /> which he also gave the name to<ref name="Kitagawa-2021" /> according to [[Motoori Norinaga]].<ref name="Cho-2022" /> He is worshipped at [[Kamochi Shrine]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kamochi Shrine {{!}} Tottori Tourism Guide |url=https://www.tottori-tour.jp/en/sightseeing/863/ |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=www.tottori-tour.jp |language=ja}}</ref> and [[Kamochi Shrine]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-21 |title=Kanemochi-Jinja Shrine - Must-See, Access, Hours & Price |url=https://www.gltjp.com/en/directory/item/12945/ |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=GOOD LUCK TRIP |language=en}}</ref> This was featured in the film ''Myths of the Izumo Province''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Myths of the Izumo Province {{!}} Search Details |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R3-00207.html |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=Japan Tourism Agency, Japan Tourism Agency |language=en}}</ref>

The antagonist of ''[[Princess Mononoke]]'' is Yatsukamizu-Omitsuno, known also as ''Shishi-gami'', {{nihongo|god of [[Hunting|prey animals]]|肉神}}. This term primarily referred to [[sika deer]] and [[wild boars]].

== Izumo expansion myth ==
He has a notable myth recorded in the ''Izumo [[Fudoki]]''.<ref name="Yatsukamizu Omitsuno" /> The myth of Omitsuno is about making Izumo bigger. He saw Izumo as a small strip of land. He decided to add more land to it. He looked towards [[Silla]] for extra land.<ref name="Antoni" /><ref name="Kitagawa-2021" /><ref name="Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo">{{Cite web |title=Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo/Exhibition/Myths in the Izumo Province |url=https://www.izm.ed.jp/english/shinwa4.html |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=www.izm.ed.jp}}</ref><ref name="The Legend of Kunibiki" />

Omitsuno used a special spade. It was shaped like a young girl's breast. He used it to cut the land. It was like cutting through fish gills. He cut off pieces of land.<ref name="Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo" /><ref name="Antoni" /><ref name="Kitagawa-2021" /><ref name="The Legend of Kunibiki" />

He attached these pieces to a three-strand rope. He pulled this land towards Izumo. He used a lot of strength. The land moved like a boat on a river. Omitsuno encouraged the land by shouting. He said, "Come on, land!"<ref name="Antoni" /><ref name="Kitagawa-2021" /><ref name="Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo" /><ref name="The Legend of Kunibiki" />

The new land went from [[Kozu Bay]] to the Cape of Kizuki. This area is known for its pure spikes.<ref name="Antoni" />
